generation.sourcePixelNote: Sheet canvas dimensions are proposals, not approved output sizes. Individual prompt width/height fields are legacy standalone fallback targets, NOT expected cell-cut dimensions. A 1536 x 1024 sheet has 512 x 512 cells before alpha trim; do not upscale cuts to those fallback sizes. Record actual output dimensions and alpha.
generation.referenceRule: Inspect every referenced source before generation. Match first approved new snow prop throughout its family. Output files do not exist merely because a prompt exists.
generation.mode: One transparent 3-column by 2-row prop sheet per generation, then cut into individually named sprites. Standalone refers to each object, not a requirement for one generation per sprite.
generation.sheetCutting: Use fixed equal cells with generous gutters, then alpha-trim each cell separately. Preserve original sheet, output each named sprite with crop/ground-anchor metadata and fitted visual size. Do not cut touching/merged objects by guesswork; reject only that cell. Import one reviewed sheet first, not all sheets at once.

density.status: proposed starting targets, not runtime configuration
density.units: visible standalone props per 1000 eligible passable world-square-units, after exclusion masks; large authored landmarks excluded
density.existingNominalExplanation: These are sums of rule inputs, NOT measured visible density. Grove masks, biome weights, trail/site clearances and blocker exclusions reduce actual counts. Do not compare raw rates directly to target observations.

targets.rule: Snowy pine/cedar groups of 3-7 in sheltered patches, sparse snow bushes/stumps/rocks around edges; broad open snow lanes and wind-scoured areas. Replace summer pine/bush stand-ins before raising counts.
Mostly grass/flowers/small stones, tree copses around field edges and rare shrines; keep open views and large clearings. Farms/hedges/sheds are authored features, not random lawn clutter.
Small rocks, upland scrub and grass in uneven rocky clusters; wind-bent trees in pockets; large outcrops rare, no unbroken obstacle walls.
Dry tussocks and scrub clustered by occasional sandstone/bleached logs; wide exposed areas, no green pine carpet or imported cactus biome.
Beach grass landward of the shore, pebbles near exposed banks, rare driftwood above the waterline. Preserve bare sand and every harbor/landing/gate approach.
Use existing grove look as the benchmark. Increase silhouette variety by importing distinct cedar/fern/stump/log sources, rather than making a uniform denser wall of the same pine.

placementRules: Seed all choices in world coordinates; retain deterministic ownership across chunk seams.
Use 20-45-unit irregular vegetation patches as a starting proposal; broad gaps matter as much as density.
Never scatter blockers on water, trails, crossings, city gate approaches, settlement/node clearances or authored clearings.
Render visual canopy extent separately from fitted trunk/rock blockers; grass, flowers and low drifts do not block walking.
Avoid adjacent repeated silhouettes at identical size; bounded scale variance around authored dimensions, no extreme random rotations of fixed-camera sprites.
Snow and dry get their own material/silhouette sets, including shores. Share temperate assets only where they actually fit.
Ground contact shading should be a shared cached treatment, not a new independently drawn effect stack for every prop.
Snow trails use packed-snow/thaw material; do not draw a brown summer dirt road through all snow.
Large landmarks are rare authored clusters with clear exits and no implied interactive systems.

samplerGuard.rule: Current paintProps chooses at most one candidate from cumulative probabilities across all biome rules, plus bamboo. Before increasing rule sums or adding coast rules, ensure sum(per1000)*grid^2/1000 stays <=1, or separately review a deterministic sampler change. Never silently clip later rules or claim raw sums equal observed density.

density.performance: Check chunk generation, active sprite count, draw calls and memory against the current accepted baseline before/after a small representative density change. Keep streamed bounds; no whole-island prop instantiation. No browser/headless automation; Tim checks in game.

shorelineKits.status: Eight orientations and distinct biome families approved for planning; exact geometry, dimensions, spans/connectors and generation prompts wait for later water design
shorelineKits.directionConvention: World-space outward water-facing direction. Every production prompt must also name its projected screen slope, which side contains land/water, its world-unit footprint and exact joining endpoints. Never rely on a filename or arbitrary sprite rotation to establish orientation.

families.materials: weathered grey stone, damp dark soil, olive bank vegetation; reusable for compatible forest/plain coasts

families.name: snow

families.name: dry
families.materials: ochre/sandstone or pale arid shore materials and dry scrub; own bank treatment, not recoloured moss

separateGeometryFamilies: coastal cliffs/rims where the blueprint calls for steep shore
shorelineKits.cornerRule: Eight facings alone do not solve arbitrary coastlines. Add compatible concave/convex connectors, caps, beach-to-cliff and biome transition joins only after the footprint/endpoint template is approved. Snow and dry share the joining template, not necessarily the silhouette or painted details.
shorelineKits.reuse: Existing numeric lake_edge_1..8 remain source candidates; they do not automatically fulfill a complete coastal or climate-specific kit.
shorelineKits.preserve: Existing usable shoreline/cliff art and screenshots remain references. New kit never changes water blockers to disguise a mismatched image.

deferred.next: Brainstorm source pools/springs/tarns/waterfalls, lake shapes and crossing geometry later; especially replace the single-diagonal source look. No copy-ready bank/bridge prompt until exact endpoints and span are approved.

Rainforest/bamboo/marsh reuse compatible existing forest/wetland art initially. Add a distinct set where material or silhouette differences justify it; do not generate eight near-identical kits by default.

ONE TRANSPARENT PROP SHEET, 3 columns by 2 rows, target 1536 x 1024 pixels, six equal 512 x 512 cells. No visible grid lines or cell borders. Each cell contains only its listed whole independent object, with at least 32 pixels of transparent padding to every cell edge and no overlap with adjacent cells. Consistent world scale: pine canopy about 5.5 world units wide; smaller bushes and rocks stay proportionately smaller, never enlarge everything to fill the cells. Maximum tree height must fit wholly inside its cell. Genuine transparent alpha, no white or painted checkerboard backdrop, text, labels, cast shadows outside objects, ground slabs, landscape, people or added objects. Per-cell dimensions below are intended in-game size after import. Keep anchors readable at the base of each object. Snow applies only to snow cells; preserve the specified palette of each biome. Do not assemble the props into one scene. Joining modules still have precisely defined connecting ends despite being separated on this sheet.

CELL 1 (top row, left): Snow-capped stone lantern. PIECE TYPE: STANDALONE. IN-GAME VISUAL GROUND COVERAGE: 1.2 x 1.2 world units. A standalone isolated prop, no joining sides. One aged Japanese stone lantern, unlit, snow on the roof and base, a little frost in the stone joints. Small isolated landmark; no paving slab, large garden or baked glow. Light, if used, is added in code.

CELL 2 (top row, middle): Abandoned snowy well. PIECE TYPE: STANDALONE. IN-GAME VISUAL GROUND COVERAGE: 2.2 x 2.2 world units. A standalone isolated prop, no joining sides. One small abandoned stone well with weathered timber crossbeam and idle bucket, rim and beam capped with snow, dark closed-looking opening. No characters, roofed building, usable water surface or background; a decorative feature with no implied new interaction.

CELL 3 (top row, right): Abandoned snowy farm shed. PIECE TYPE: STANDALONE. IN-GAME VISUAL GROUND COVERAGE: 6 x 4 world units. A standalone isolated prop, no joining sides. One small ruined rural timber farm shed, partially collapsed roof, dark weathered posts, a few visible rafters and snow on the remaining roof. A single coherent ruin; no yard, fences, field, scattered distant debris or habitable interior. Fixed facing matching existing Japanese buildings.

CELL 4 (bottom row, left): Snowy farm fence, x axis. PIECE TYPE: JOINING PIECE. IN-GAME VISUAL GROUND COVERAGE: 6 x 0.35 world units. JOINING SIDES: -x and +x. A straight 6-world-unit rustic timber farm-fence module, about 1.1 units high. Its ground baseline runs upper-left to lower-right on screen, a slope of exactly 1 vertical for 2 horizontal. Joining ends: both ends along the x axis must meet identical modules at equal ground level and rail height. Use two simple weathered horizontal rails, snow caps and sparse connecting posts; end posts are half shared so adjoining pieces do not form oversized doubled posts. No endcaps, corner turn, gate, enclosed yard, curved fence or background. Match the other axis companion's posts, rails, snow and physical proportions.

CELL 5 (bottom row, middle): Snowy farm fence, z axis. PIECE TYPE: JOINING PIECE. IN-GAME VISUAL GROUND COVERAGE: 0.35 x 6 world units. JOINING SIDES: -z and +z.
